title: Harden the unattended 3-loop autonomy story (sweep + debate gaps)
description:
Make running the loop family (`/code` + `/land` + `/epic-audit`) safe UNATTENDED by
adding the one missing leg — an exception surfacer — and closing the real gaps a
`/debate` pass surfaced. Today `/code -> /land` runs reliably, but two pipeline
outputs have NO downstream consumer: `land-escalated` branches and `human`-labeled
decision tickets. Nothing pings a human when work parks on a decision; you only find
it by manually running `bd`.

## Where this came from
Design pass captured in scratchpad `sweep-spec.md` (the `/sweep` skill, v2) and
`debate-agenda.md` (companion changes), then stress-tested by `/debate`. The debate
REVERSED several of the original agenda items — this epic encodes the debate's honest
build list, not the original wishlist.

## Debate verdict (what actually holds)
- The unattended story HOLDS. Its real load-bearing assumption is that concurrent
  `bd dolt push` from the existing N-producer fan-out is safe — NOT any new lock.
  ("single-lander lock" guards `trunk`, not Dolt; the system is already many-writer
  to Dolt by design.)
- The ONE genuine upstream gap: `land-escalated` has no defined resolution transition
  — the queue never drains.
- Epic auto-close and the bounce/rebase caps are OVER-ENGINEERING or YAGNI — DEFER
  them (see this epic's Design field). The surfacer IS the detector.

## Build list (children)
1. `/sweep` skill — surface-only human-decision surfacer, cross-machine-safe dedup.
2. Define the `land-escalated` resolution transition in `/land` (the real gap).
3. Validate concurrent `bd dolt push` under the `/code` N-producer fan-out.
4. Record the debate decisions in `docs/` (per CLAUDE.md, design facts live in docs/,
   not tickets/memory).
design:
SETTLED BY DEBATE (these are decisions, to be mirrored into docs/ by child #4):

DECIDED — DO:
- Build `/sweep` surface-only. Scope = surface the human-decision queue
  (`bd list --label land-escalated` ∪ `bd human list`) + epics that are
  `epic-audited` + open + all-children-closed ("ready for a human to close").
  NO audit dispatch (that is already `/loop /epic-audit`). NO decisions made.
- Dedup store = the digest issue ITSELF (Dolt-durable, travels cross-machine).
  A scratchpad state file re-notifies the whole queue from a second machine — rejected.
- Fix the real gap: define how a human clears a `land-escalated` (child #2).

DECIDED — DEFER (captured, NOT to be built until evidence appears; do NOT file as
ready children — that would contradict the debate and let `/code` build them):
- `/land` bounce-lineage cap (bounce_depth counter → escalate after N). Mechanism is
  sound (`--set-metadata bounce_depth`, survives supersede), but no bounce-chain has
  been OBSERVED. The `/sweep` digest IS the detector; add the cap when a real chain
  shows up. See debate-agenda.md §A.
- `/code` rebase-attempt cap. Churn-only failure; a real rebase conflict already
  escapes to `land-escalated`. YAGNI. See debate-agenda.md §B.
- Epic AUTO-CLOSE + confirming re-audit. REJECTED, not merely deferred: epic closure
  is a human capability-judgment; auto-close trades a high-cost false "done" to save
  one rare click. Each gap child already passes code-review + land-review + land gate,
  so a re-audit only re-does judgment a human should own. Manual `/epic-audit <id>`
  already re-verifies on demand. See debate-agenda.md §C.

DECIDED — REFRAME:
- The "bd-write concurrency / shared lock" agenda item is a category error (guards
  trunk, not Dolt). The only real question is whether concurrent `bd dolt push` under
  the existing N-producer fan-out is safe — a PRE-EXISTING property, filed as child #3,
  not a `/sweep` blocker. `/sweep` writes one self-owned digest row → cannot contend.
acceptance_criteria: /sweep exists and surfaces the human-decision queue (land-escalated + bd human list) plus close-ready epics, with cross-machine-safe dedup; land-escalated has a defined resolution transition so the queue drains; concurrent bd dolt push under /code fan-out is validated (or a follow-up bug filed); all debate decisions recorded in docs/.
notes:
EMBEDDED DEBATE AGENDA (verbatim, source of record — replaces scratchpad/debate-agenda.md; covers the deferred/rejected caps + the concurrency reframing):

# Debate agenda — the 3-loop autonomy story

Companion to [`sweep-spec.md`](./sweep-spec.md). Package for `/debate`: one
concrete change (the `/land` bounce cap) plus the cross-cutting questions that
surfaced while reading the `land` / `epic-audit` skills. Nothing here is built.

The framing to debate: **`/sweep` makes livelocks *visible*; caps make them
*impossible*.** Do we ship surface-only (v1) or surface + prevent (bigger)?

---

## A. COMPANION CHANGE (drafted) — `/land` bounce-lineage cap

**The problem it closes.** A bounce supersedes the ticket and opens a rebuild
ticket (`/land` SKILL.md §"Bounce", lines 324-364). If `land-review` bounces the
rebuild for the same reason, you get an **unbounded supersede chain** — a real
internal livelock, needing no external churn. There is no cap today; the only
escape is a rebuild finally passing or a human noticing.

**The change.** Carry a `bounce_depth` on the lineage. On the Nth bounce, stop
rebuilding and **escalate** instead — routing the stuck lineage into the same
`land-escalated` queue `/sweep` surfaces. Local to `/land`'s Bounce section:

```bash
BOUNCE_CAP=${BOUNCE_CAP:-3}                       # tunable; 3 rebuild attempts then hand to a human
DEPTH=$(rtk bd show <id> --json | jq -r '.[0].metadata.bounce_depth // 0')

if [ "$DEPTH" -ge "$BOUNCE_CAP" ]; then
  # Lineage has failed land-review $DEPTH times — this is no longer a "rebuild",
  # it's a genuine "a human must break this loop". Escalate, keep the branch+findings.
  rtk bd update <id> --add-label land-escalated --remove-label ready-for-land \
    --append-notes "BOUNCE CAP ($DEPTH ≥ $BOUNCE_CAP): lineage bounced repeatedly without landing.
Latest land-review findings: <findings>. A human must decide: is the acceptance
achievable as written, is land-review wrong, or should this epic child be dropped?"
  rtk bd dolt push
  # NOTE: branch KEPT (like any escalate) so the human has the artifact.
else
  # ... existing bounce flow (create NEW, re-parent, re-point deps, supersede) ...
  NEW=$(rtk bd create ... --json | jq -r '.id')
  rtk bd update "$NEW" --set-metadata bounce_depth=$((DEPTH+1))   # repo convention (coding.md uses --set-metadata for land_head etc.); value stored as a string, bash -ge reads it numerically
  # ... rest of existing bounce flow ...
fi
```

**Debate targets for this change:**
1. **Counter vs. chain-walk.** A `bounce_depth` metadata counter is simplest and
   self-contained, but is manual state. Alternative: walk the `supersede` chain
   (`bd` links `<id> -> NEW`) and count depth from the graph — no counter, but
   depends on the chain being cleanly walkable. Which is more robust?
2. **Cap value.** 3? 2? Too low = premature human interrupts on legitimately
   iterative work; too high = tokens burned on a doomed lineage.
3. **Keep or drop the branch on cap-escalate?** Escalate normally keeps the
   branch. Here the branch is judged bad-as-is — but the human still wants the
   artifact + findings. Draft keeps it; is that right?
4. **Does the cap belong in `/land` or `land-review`?** `land-review` produces
   the bounce verdict; `/land` executes it. The depth is a landing-loop concern,
   so the draft puts it in `/land` — agree?
5. **Sequencing:** ship this WITH `/sweep`, or ship `/sweep` first (surface-only)
   and add the cap once a real bounce-chain is observed?

---

## B. SMALLER SIBLING (sketch) — `/code` rebase-attempt cap

Same pattern, lower priority. `needs-rebase` starvation is **theoretical** —
only under perpetual trunk churn; a finite backlog quiesces, and a real rebase
*conflict* already escapes to `land-escalated` (`/land` line 322). A
`rebase_attempts` counter in `/code`'s needs-rebase sweep, escalating after N,
would bound even the perpetual-churn case. **Question for debate: is this worth
building at all, or is the churn-only failure mode too rare to guard?**

---

## C. POLICY QUESTION — epic close + re-audit of filed gaps

`/epic-audit` **never closes an epic** (line 156) and, after filing gap children,
does **not** re-arm — re-auditing is a manual `/epic-audit <epic>` (line 155). So
after an audit's gaps are built and landed:

- nothing **re-audits** to confirm the gaps actually filled the holes, and
- nothing **closes** the epic — it sits `epic-audited` + open forever until a
  human closes it (`/sweep` will now *surface* this, but not resolve it).

**Debate:**
1. Is "a human closes every epic" the right permanent policy, or should there be
   an **auto-close** when `epic-audited` + all children closed + a *clean*
   confirming re-audit?
2. If gaps were filed, should landing the last gap child **re-arm exactly one**
   confirming audit — and how do we do that *without* reopening the regeneration
   loop the `epic-audited` terminal label currently prevents? (e.g. a distinct
   `epic-reaudit-pending` label that grants exactly one more pass.)
3. Or is manual re-audit the correct, deliberate human checkpoint — keep it?

---

## D. CROSS-CUTTING — running three loops unattended

1. **Quiescence / poll cost.** `/code`, `/land`, `/epic-audit`(, `/sweep`) poll
   forever; a no-op tick still spends a model turn. Do we want adaptive backoff
   or a quiescence stop ("N passes, all queues empty, no new tickets → stop") for
   the loop family, or is fixed-interval polling an acceptable cost?
2. **bd-write concurrency.** `/land` guards itself with a *land-specific*
   lockfile; `/epic-audit` and `/sweep` have none. On one machine that's three
   `bd dolt push` writers (plus parallel subagents). Do they need a **shared
   bd-write lock**, or is one-machine turn-interleaving + Dolt's own conflict
   handling enough? This is the operational risk of adding a third writer.
3. **One machine, three loops — is that the intended topology?** `/land`'s
   single-writer guarantee is a one-machine convention. `/code` fans out
   producers (possibly cross-machine). Does adding `/sweep` + `/epic-audit`
   pressure the "everything landing-side on one machine" assumption?

---

## Suggested debate order

1. **C** and **D** are the biggest-leverage — they're about whether the
   *unattended* story actually holds, independent of `/sweep`'s shape.
2. **A** — is the bounce cap worth building now (surface + prevent) vs. later.
3. `sweep-spec.md` open questions — only after the above settle its scope.
4. **B** — smallest; may be a "won't build".
CRITICISM (/debate 2026-07-08) — EPIC-LEVEL COMPLETENESS GAP:
1. TWO OF THE DEBATE'S OWN 'BIGGEST-LEVERAGE' QUESTIONS DROPPED WITHOUT DISPOSITION. The embedded agenda calls C and D the biggest-leverage items. The epic records dispositions for A (defer), B (defer), C (reject), D.2 (reframe -> child .3). But D.1 (poll/quiescence cost — do the loops back off or stop when all queues empty, or is fixed-interval polling accepted?) and D.3 (is 'all three loops on one machine' the intended topology, given /land's single-writer guarantee is a one-machine convention while /code may fan out cross-machine?) have NO recorded disposition — not in the epic Design, not in child .4's record list. Adding /sweep as a THIRD forever-polling loop directly implicates both. This is exactly the 'forks the record' failure the project warns against. RESOLVE: give D.1 and D.3 an explicit disposition (decide/defer-with-rationale/reject) and add them to .4's record list, or state in the epic why they're out of scope. [DECISION PENDING x2 - surfaced to human]
DECISIONS (human, 2026-07-08) — epic completeness gap RESOLVED:
- D.1 (poll/quiescence cost): DEFER (deferred-but-not-forgotten). Fixed-interval polling stands; adaptive backoff / quiescence-stop ('N empty passes -> stop') is revisited only if no-op poll cost is OBSERVED to matter. Record in docs/decisions.md.
- D.3 (topology): DECIDED. INVARIANT — the landing-side loops (/land + /epic-audit + /sweep) run on ONE machine; /code producers MAY fan out cross-machine (they write disjoint Dolt rows + push branches only). This makes /land's single-writer guarantee an explicit stated invariant, not an implicit convention. Record in docs/decisions.md. (Distributed refs/locks/land stays deferred — NOT un-deferred.)

title: E-TUI feedback — expose ids, introspect enrichment, work-to-completion, quieter logs, readable dates
description: Tracks the five feedback items in specs/03-tui-features.md (current-work feedback after E11 TUI + async queue landed): (1) expose note id for purge via TUI Browse + a CLI list command; (2) make enrichment outcomes visible to the end user; (3) a 'work to completion' option that polls/blocks until submitted jobs are processed; (4) stop mirroring httpx 200-OK lines to stdout/stderr from work/ask — errors only; (5) shorter, human-readable dates in Browse. Children filed per item after disambiguation.
design:
## Success Criteria

- purge is usable end-to-end: a user can find a note's id (CLI list + TUI Browse) and hard-delete it, ideally by a short prefix.
- Enrichment outcomes are visible: after `work`, and on demand per-note, the user can see what tags/entities/summary/edges/embeds a note got.
- `lode work` has an opt-in mode that blocks until submitted jobs are fully processed (bounded by a timeout).
- `work` and `ask` no longer mirror httpx 200-OK lines to stderr; only actionable errors surface.
- Browse dates are short and human-readable (adaptive absolute), not full ISO-8601 timestamps.

## Design notes (post-disambiguation, specs/03-tui-features.md)

- Item 2: build the in-flow `work` summary + a `lode show <id>` CLI. NOT the TUI note-view panel and NOT enrich-counts-in-jobs.
- Item 5: adaptive absolute format (time today / weekday+time this week / mon+day this year / ISO year older).
- Item 1: 8-char id column in Browse + full id on NoteViewScreen + purge-by-unambiguous-prefix.
close_reason: Epic complete: all 8 children landed on trunk; /epic-audit clean bill (5/5 success criteria satisfied, no gaps). Closed by human direction.

title: E15 — 02-feedback: logging telemetry cleanup, --debug flag, save-on-exit popup
description:
Tracks the four feedback items in specs/02-feedback.md (trunk snapshot 3c2f365; current trunk 59b5018): two logging items (undocumented LODE_LOG_LEVEL; debug logs corrupting the TUI console), a new top-level --debug CLI flag to enable diagnostic instrumentation, and a UX fix so the save-on-exit confirm is a popup over the editor instead of a full blank screen.

## Design decisions (confirmed with user 2026-07-04; refined after /debate)
- Item 3 (lode-1i8.2) = TUI-ONLY file logging. Suppress console/stderr log output only while the TUI runs, keeping the file handler (and guaranteeing one is attached so Python's lastResort can't fire). Plain CLI commands (ask/add) KEEP stderr — 'lode ask' deliberately mirrors an AuthError's cause to stderr; that path is preserved. (Re-scoped from an earlier 'drop stderr globally' after debate flagged the CLI regression.)
- Item 2 (lode-1i8.3) = TOP-LEVEL 'lode --debug' flag on the root Typer callback: sets DEBUG log level + enables diagnostic instrumentation (event-loop-lag probe, etc.) for every subcommand. Accepted coupling: --debug == DEBUG log level (verbosity == feature-enablement); split later if needed.
- Item 4 (lode-1i8.4) = external Textual .tcss stylesheet (repo's first), wired via CSS_PATH and shipped via pyproject package-data.

## Sequencing
- .2 blocks .3 (shared logconfig/cli files).
- .1 blocks .3 (both edit docs/configuration.md — avoid merge collision; .3 appends to the logging section .1 creates).
- .4 is independent.

Related prior epic lode-0wj (E14) delivered the exit-safety confirm guard (lode-0wj.1 Escape, lode-0wj.8 Ctrl+Q) and the lag-diagnosis spike (lode-0wj.2) whose probe is gated on DEBUG; item 4 here refines that confirm UX.

## Success Criteria
- LODE_LOG_LEVEL (and ANTHROPIC_LOG) documented in docs/configuration.md.
- A top-level 'lode --debug' flag raises log level to DEBUG and enables diagnostic instrumentation across all subcommands.
- Running 'lode tui' writes ZERO log output to the terminal (console suppressed for the TUI session, file handler retained), so latency telemetry is collectible via the log file without corrupting the TUI; plain CLI stderr logging is unchanged.
- Pressing Escape (or Ctrl+Q) over a dirty capture buffer shows a centered popup dialog (external .tcss, shipped in the wheel) over the still-visible editor; Cancel dismisses it and returns to the editor unchanged.
close_reason: E15 complete: all 5 children landed; epic-audit (manual re-audit) confirmed all four Success Criteria delivered on trunk (LODE_LOG_LEVEL/ANTHROPIC_LOG docs, lode --debug flag, TUI console suppression, save-on-exit popup); deferred --debug↔DEBUG coupling decision recorded in docs/decisions.md.

title: Instrument the capture screen: reveal what runs during input (lag diagnosis spike)
description: Feedback: typing feels laggy/blocked and it's unclear what the app does behind the scenes. Add lightweight, toggleable instrumentation (timing/logging around the event loop, keystroke->render latency, and the passive related-notes worker: how often it fires, how long find_related_notes / the ONNX embedder / LanceDB take, whether passes overlap). Prime suspect: on_text_area_changed debounces a pass that runs the embedder+LanceDB via asyncio.to_thread on every idle pause. Goal is DATA, not a fix: identify what actually blocks input. Blocks the optimisation follow-up.
acceptance_criteria: REPRO PRECONDITION: reproduce the felt lag against a realistic seeded corpus (reuse the deterministic seed-corpus fixture from lode-5y8.4), NOT an empty DB — an empty/small DB makes the related-notes pass return instantly and hides the lag. Define a target keystroke->render latency (e.g. p95 threshold) so the spike has a pass/fail, not just 'notes'. MUST-ANSWER: does the passive related-notes worker actually yield the event loop? i.e. does the fastembed/ONNX embed release the GIL during inference — asyncio.to_thread only relieves input if it does; if ONNX holds the GIL the 'background' pass stalls typing anyway. Deliverable: findings on this ticket (what runs on the input path, measured cost, and the GIL/event-loop-yield verdict). No behaviour change beyond instrumentation.
notes:
Debate (lode-0wj): the prime suspect (related-notes pass) is ALREADY off the UI thread via asyncio.to_thread + @work(exclusive=True) in src/lode/tui/screens/capture.py, so on paper it should not block input. The one mechanism that WOULD make it block: to_thread does not help if the offloaded C code holds the GIL — fastembed/ONNX inference may not release it. Verifying that is the load-bearing question for whether lode-0wj.3 (disable related-notes) is the right fix or a red herring.
FINDINGS (spike, git 96e2c19, tests/test_capture_lag_diagnosis.py, opt-in LODE_DIAGNOSE_LAG=1):

Reproduced against the REAL lode-5y8.4 seed corpus (10 notes) with the REAL
fastembed/ONNX embedder (not the eval scorer's offline hash stub) -- an empty
DB was avoided per the acceptance precondition.

PASS/FAIL TARGET: p95 event-loop tick lag < 100ms during the pass (the
standard "feels instant" interactive-response threshold), measured as how much
longer a 10ms asyncio.sleep heartbeat comes back late by -- a direct proxy for
keystroke->render latency since Textual's key handling/repaint run on the same
event loop.

MUST-ANSWER, DIRECT RESULT: YES, fastembed/ONNX DOES release the GIL during
inference, and asyncio.to_thread IS relieving input as designed.
  - find_related_notes cost against the seeded corpus: min=52-63ms
    mean=64-68ms p95=70-76ms max=70-76ms (5 realistic mid-typing drafts).
  - Event-loop lag, full find_related_notes pass (FTS5+ONNX+LanceDB) via
    asyncio.to_thread, sustained over 10 repeated passes: idle baseline
    p95=0.3-0.4ms; DURING the pass p95=5.2-7.7ms, max=5.8-9.6ms. Comfortably
    under the 100ms target -- PASS.
  - Isolated to embedder.embed_query alone (no DB/LanceDB, ONNX only): idle
    p95=0.4-0.5ms; during embed p95=1.2-1.5ms, max=2.2-2.4ms. PASS, and
    confirms the (small) lag above is not concentrated in ONNX specifically.

INTERPRETATION: the passive related-notes worker is NOT the mechanism behind
the felt lag. It already runs off the UI thread via asyncio.to_thread +
@work(exclusive=True) (structurally can't overlap -- a new pass cancels/
supersedes any still-running one), and the offloaded call (FTS5 + fastembed/
ONNX + LanceDB combined) yields the event loop well within the pass/fail
target. This is evidence AGAINST the prime suspect the lode-0wj debate raised:
lode-0wj.3 (disable/opt-in the passive pass) is likely a red herring as
currently scoped and should be re-evaluated against other candidates (Textual
render cost, TextArea internals, terminal I/O, something outside this pass)
before being treated as the fix -- lode-0wj.4 (optimise based on findings)
should look elsewhere first.

Caveat: this spike measured a *single* related-notes pass's cost per call, not
compounding effects from many other things happening concurrently in a real
long TUI session (job queue worker, reconciliation scan, etc.) -- if the felt
lag persists after lode-0wj.4 investigates other candidates, re-run this
spike's heartbeat instrumentation (now permanent, DEBUG-gated, in
lode.tui.latency_probe + lode.tui.screens.capture) against a live session to
see if some other component holds the GIL longer.

INSTRUMENTATION (permanent, toggleable, no behaviour change): DEBUG-level
logging in lode.tui.screens.capture around debounce restart/fire and each
related-notes pass (sequence number, duration, result count, whether it was
cancelled by a newer pass), plus lode.tui.latency_probe.probe_event_loop_lag,
an event-loop-lag heartbeat only started while
log.isEnabledFor(logging.DEBUG). All gated behind LODE_LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG
(existing lode.logconfig convention) -- zero log calls and zero extra worker
at the default INFO level.

Reproduction: LODE_DIAGNOSE_LAG=1 pytest -s tests/test_capture_lag_diagnosis.py

metadata.land_summary: Lag-diagnosis spike (lode-0wj.2): DEBUG-gated event-loop-lag instrumentation (lode.tui.latency_probe + capture screen) + opt-in seeded-corpus repro; verdict: fastembed/ONNX releases the GIL, related-notes pass is not the felt-lag cause. No behaviour change at INFO.

title: Confirm-on-unsaved guard for the capture screen's Escape (stop Escape silently discarding)
description: ASSUMED DECISION (proceeding without user confirm — revisit if wrong): scope to ESCAPE ONLY — fully screen-local, directly solves the vi-muscle-memory footgun. Escape on a dirty (non-empty/non-whitespace) capture buffer pops a Save/Discard/Cancel confirm; an empty buffer exits immediately so get-in/dump/get-out stays fast. Ctrl+S keeps its direct save+exit. The app-level Ctrl+Q confirm-if-dirty is SPLIT OUT to lode-0wj.8: Ctrl+Q is a global App binding (priority=True, src/lode/tui/app.py) and cannot be guarded from inside the capture screen. 'Dirty' == non-empty buffer today (capture only ever mints a NEW note; 'unchanged vs empty' only becomes a real distinction once lode-0wj.6 loads an existing version into the buffer).
acceptance_criteria: Escape on a non-empty/non-whitespace capture buffer shows a Save/Discard/Cancel confirm; Discard exits, Save saves+exits, Cancel returns to editing. Escape on an empty/whitespace-only buffer exits with no prompt. Ctrl+S behaviour unchanged. Tests cover dirty vs empty for Escape.

metadata.land_summary: Capture screen: Escape on a dirty buffer pops a Save/Discard/Cancel confirm (DiscardConfirmScreen); empty/whitespace buffer still exits immediately; Ctrl+S unchanged. Tests cover all legs.

title: E14 — Post-E11 TUI feedback: exit safety, input latency, browse screen
description: Tracks user feedback gathered after E11 (TUI screens) shipped. Three themes from specs/01-feedback.md: (1) too easy to lose work — Escape silently discards the capture buffer (vi muscle-memory hits it), want a safer exit (Ctrl+Q and/or confirm-on-unsaved); (2) TUI is laggy — input feels blocked, need instrumentation to find the cause and optimisations (likely the passive related-notes pass and/or async task scheduling); (3) browsing interface — add an opt-in browse screen listing notes (Date/Version/Summary), selecting opens a note, Escape returns to the list; viewing prior versions deferred. Children filed under this epic.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Neither Escape nor the app-level quit key can silently discard an unsaved capture buffer (scope of the quit-key guard resolved in lode-0wj.1). 2) The TUI has instrumentation that reveals what runs on the input path (incl. whether background passes actually yield the event loop), and at least one MEASURED optimisation lands against a defined latency threshold so typing no longer feels blocked. 3) A browse screen lists notes and lets the user open one and return, without adding overhead to the default get-in/dump/get-out capture path.
notes: Source: specs/01-feedback.md. Grounding: capture screen binds escape->discard (src/lode/tui/screens/capture.py); app binds ctrl+q->quit (src/lode/tui/app.py); passive related-notes runs ONNX embedder+LanceDB per idle pause via asyncio.to_thread.
close_reason: E14 fully delivered — all 11 children landed and tested; epic-audit clean bill (exit safety, measured ~14x TUI latency fix, browse screen all satisfy acceptance). Closed by user after audit.

title: Skeleton not end-to-end: restore synchronous inline embed in capture path; prove lode add -> lode ask via real CLI (no in-test stand-in)
description: GAP (found 2026-06-28): the Phase-A skeleton does NOT work end-to-end through the real CLI. "lode add" enqueues embed/enrich derive jobs (jobs.enqueue_derive_jobs, lode-y42.1) but NOTHING drains them: E2 (lode-i05.*) is unbuilt and embedding does NOT run inline either. A real "lode add" then "lode ask" therefore retrieves nothing (empty passages/vectors) and abstains. The exit-gate pass (lode-6w1.1) is masked: tests/test_skeleton_gate.py defines its own _run_derive_job() that runs embed() synchronously with a stub embedder INSIDE the test, so it never exercises any user-runnable processing step. This contradicts the epic (lode-6w1), which specified "synchronous inline embed (no queue yet)" for the skeleton: lode-x6r.2 built the embed(version) function and lode-x6r.5 is the deepening that MOVES it to the async queue once E2 exists. The build skipped ahead to enqueue-only without the drain. FIX (skeleton, simplest thing that works): make "lode add" run chunk+embed inline (lode-x6r.2 intent) so capture makes the note findable; keep the durable embed/enrich enqueue as the E2 seam but do NOT make the skeleton ask depend on a worker. Then replace the in-test stand-in with a CLI-level test that proves a real "lode add" followed by "lode ask" yields a verbatim-grounded cited claim and that an out-of-corpus question abstains. Do NOT build the full async worker here: that stays E2 (lode-i05.3, P2) and the inline->async move stays lode-x6r.5.

title: CLI enrichment parity: 'lode show' consumes the shared view-model + pending state
description: Bring 'lode show' to CONTENT parity with the new TUI modal by routing it through the ay5.1 view-model instead of its own display.py calls, so the two surfaces cannot diverge as enrichment grows. Net user-visible CLI changes (decisions 2026-07-08): (a) EDGES gain reason+confidence — 'lode show' prints only '-> to_id [stale]' TODAY; it must render the compact form '-> to_id (reason, 0.82)[stale]' to match the view-model; (b) ENRICHMENT_STATE — a three-valued line {pending, failed, ready} replaces the ambiguous bare '(none)', so a not-yet-enriched note reads 'enrichment: pending', a dead-lettered one 'enrichment: failed', both distinct from enriched-but-empty. No new CLI command (per user note 'track the CLI work to ensure parity ... but that's all on that side') — but NOT a pure thin refactor: it adds the two fields above.
design: Refactor cli.show_ to build the ay5.1 EnrichmentView and render from it (summary/tags/entities/edges/embed/enrichment_state), preserving current wording where it already matches (stale suffix, '(none)' for genuinely-empty sections). NEW output vs today: (1) edges render compactly WITH reason+confidence ('-> to_id (reason, conf)[stale]') — today's cli.show_ prints only '-> to_id [stale]'; (2) an enrichment_state line renders {pending | failed | ready} — an explicit 'enrichment: pending'/'enrichment: failed' rather than a '(none)' that reads identical to enriched-empty. Keep 'lode notes' as-is unless the summary/state signal is trivially reusable there. PARITY GUARD (decision 2026-07-08): CONTENT parity = same view-model FIELDS surfaced on both, NOT byte-identical output; the regression test enumerates the view-model's fields and asserts 'lode show' surfaces each (and that pending/failed/empty are wording-distinct), rather than diffing against the modal's exact bytes.
acceptance_criteria: 'lode show' renders from the ay5.1 view-model (no independent display.py assembly); it surfaces every view-model field incl. edge reason+confidence (compact) and a three-valued enrichment_state; an un-enriched note reads 'pending' and a dead-lettered one 'failed', both distinct from enriched-empty; a CLI test enumerates the view-model fields and asserts each is surfaced, and that pending/failed/empty wording is distinct (content parity by field-coverage, not byte-identical to the modal).
notes:
CRITICISM (debate 2026-07-08):
1. 'Thin refactor + one pending line' is wrong if the parity target includes edge reason+confidence — cli.show_ prints neither today, so that parity option makes this a net-new user-visible CLI change. Re-scope once the epic decides the edge parity field-set. Blocked on the lode-ay5 crux decision.
2. Its parity test asserts the CLI renders the view-model's fields, but NOT that CLI output matches the modal. See lode-ay5 note 3.

title: TUI enrichment inspector modal on Browse ('i' → modal, Esc dismiss)

On the notes DataTable, 'i' on the highlighted row opens a ModalScreen rendering that note's enrichment via the ay5.1 view-model (summary, tags, entities, inferred edges with confidence+reason+stale flag, embed status, and a three-valued enrichment_state indicator: 'pending' when not yet enriched, 'failed' when the enrich job dead-lettered, else the enriched/ready content; stale last-known content is shown alongside a 'pending' re-enrich). Esc dismisses back to the list. The modal may grow/scroll over the list body for long content. The capture screen is NOT touched. Register/style consistent with the existing DiscardConfirmScreen ModalScreen pattern + lode.tcss. Follows the same 'i'-on-highlighted-row mechanics as the existing 'e' (edit) binding in BrowseScreen.
design: ModalScreen (dim-behind, like DiscardConfirmScreen) pushed from BrowseScreen.action_inspect_selected, keyed to the highlighted row's note_id via coordinate_to_cell_key (same accessor 'e' uses). Content is a scroll container so long summaries/edge lists expand over the list rather than truncating; Esc = pop_screen (one level, same contract as the rest of the browse family). Renders ONLY ay5.1's view-model — no DB/policy logic in the screen. Add the 'i' Binding to BrowseScreen.BINDINGS with a Footer label 'Inspect'. Optional stretch: also bind 'i' on NoteViewScreen for the already-open note (symmetry) — keep Browse-triggered as the primary, do not expand scope if it complicates the modal. Update docs/configuration.md TUI section (or the relevant doc) noting the new introspection surface, in-worktree at build time.

CRITICISM (debate 2026-07-08):
1. Plumbing verified SOUND — DiscardConfirmScreen is a real ModalScreen (capture.py) and coordinate_to_cell_key is the exact accessor 'e' uses. No blocker on mechanics.
2. Parity: pilot tests assert the modal renders view-model fields but don't guard against CLI/modal divergence (see lode-ay5 note 3). If edges show reason/confidence here but 'lode show' omits them, the surfaces silently diverge.

title: Enrichment view-model reader (shared TUI+CLI seam)
description: A pure read function (no Textual, no Typer) that assembles a note's full enrichment view for display: given (db_path/conn, note_id) return summary, tags, entities, inferred edges (each with to_id, reason, confidence, stale flag), embed status, AND a three-valued enrichment_state {pending, ready, failed} keyed on the head version — distinguishing not-yet-enriched (pending) from enriched-empty (ready) from dead-lettered (failed). Built ENTIRELY on lode.display.display_annotations/display_edges (the shared stale-display policy, lode-npx.4) plus the embed check 'lode show' already does — this is the single seam both the TUI modal (ay5.2) and the CLI parity guard (ay5.3) consume, so they cannot drift. Unit-testable in isolation with a seeded SQLite db.
design:
Return a small frozen dataclass (EnrichmentView) rather than a dict so both consumers get typed fields. Payloads: tag/entity/summary are bare strings; edges carry to_id + reason + confidence + stale. Embed status from the head's passages count (as cli.show_ does today).

CONTENT (decision 2026-07-08): always via display_annotations(note_id)/display_edges(note_id) — note_id-scoped, spanning versions, stale items flagged, tombstones/hidden-assertive dropped (the lode-npx.4 policy verbatim, no second copy of classify_*). Content is NEVER suppressed by state.

STATE — enrichment_state is THREE-valued {pending, ready, failed}, keyed on the HEAD version (decisions 2026-07-08):
  - pending: head's target_version has a live (pending/running) 'enrich' job.
  - failed: head has a dead/failed 'enrich' job (no live one) AND zero source='ai' rows for head's source_version — a dead-letter surfaced honestly, NOT as enriched-empty.
  - ready: otherwise (head has source='ai' rows, or genuinely no job).
This makes not-yet-run, ran-and-failed, and ran-and-empty all distinguishable (async enrichment makes empty sections ambiguous today). Because content is note_id-scoped and state is head-keyed, a re-enriching note legitimately reports state=pending WITH stale last-known content shown — that co-occurrence is intended.

No writes.
acceptance_criteria: A documented reader returns the assembled enrichment view for a note_id, reusing lode.display verbatim (no second copy of classify_*), with a THREE-valued enrichment_state {pending, ready, failed} keyed on the head; covered by unit tests over a seeded db including: enriched (ready) note, un-enriched (pending) note, dead-lettered (failed) note, a re-enriching note that reports state=pending WITH stale content shown, a note with stale items, and a tombstoned edge case.
notes:
CRITICISM (debate 2026-07-08):
1. pending/empty flag ignores a third real state — failed/dead. Predicate 'pending job OR zero ai rows -> pending; else enriched' misclassifies a dead-lettered enrich job (zero ai rows, no live job) as 'enriched-empty'. jobs.status has failed/dead terminals; schema says the UI surfaces 'dead' as dead-letters. DECISION: add a third state to EnrichmentView, or explicitly scope dead-letters out.
2. Predicate couples two row identities. display_annotations keys WHERE target=note_id; pending keys on the head version (jobs.target_version, ai rows source_version=head). After an edit, old-head ai rows (target=note_id) render stale via display while the new head has zero ai + a pending job -> the note is simultaneously 'stale content' AND 'pending'. Pin the exact predicate IN THIS TICKET (not 'at build time'); it determines whether pending+stale can co-occur in one render.
DECISION (2026-07-08, note 1 resolved): THREE-STATE view-model. enrichment_state in {pending, ready, failed}. A dead/failed enrich job with no source='ai' rows for the head surfaces as 'failed' (dead-lettered), distinct from pending and from ready-but-empty. Rationale (user): 'Honesty is better; gives the TUI user a basis for action.' Both surfaces (modal + lode show) render the failed state, not a misleading '(none)'.
DECISION (2026-07-08, note 2 resolved — PREDICATE PINNED): State keyed on HEAD version; content always shown.
- enrichment_state: 'pending' iff head's target_version has a live (pending/running) enrich job; 'failed' iff head has a dead/failed enrich job (no live one) AND zero source='ai' rows for head's source_version; else 'ready'.
- content: always display_annotations(note_id)/display_edges(note_id) as-is, stale items flagged — NEVER suppressed by state.
- Consequence: a re-enriching note shows enrichment_state=pending AND its stale last-known enrichment together (pending + stale COEXIST). Honors the stale-display policy (show-flagged, never hide).

title: [epic] Surface enrichment in the TUI (with CLI parity)
description: Close the 'introspect / surface enrichment' gap. Enrichment produces a summary, tags, entities (annotations) and inferred edges (edges, each carrying reason+confidence in the DB), plus embed status — but the TUI surfaces NONE of it, and the CLI only PARTIALLY does. 'lode show' (specs/03 item 2, lode-1gr.5, DONE) prints summary/tags/entities and edge TARGETS (with a [stale] flag) but NOT edge reason/confidence, and cannot distinguish not-yet-enriched from enriched-empty. A user who captures a note in the TUI and browses it can read the body and version chain but cannot see what enrichment landed. This epic adds a TUI introspection surface, routes both surfaces through ONE shared read seam (a view-model built on lode.display), and brings the CLI up to the same field set — CONTENT parity, not byte-identical output (each surface formats for its medium). NOT a revisit of specs/03 (that shipped 'lode show'); the intent 'introspect/surface enrichment' is broader than the CLI slice already closed.
design: INTERACTION (user decision 2026-07-08, chosen from ASCII mock-ups): enrichment introspection is a MODAL on top of the Browse list (F3), opened with 'i' on the highlighted row and dismissed with Esc — a fast glance-and-dismiss, no need to open the note body first. The modal may expand/scroll over the list body for long content. CONSTRAINTS: the capture screen stays untouched (capture must remain fast/distraction-free); introspection lives ONLY on the Browse/explore side — capture and explore are orthogonal. CONTENT: summary, tags, entities, inferred edges (each with confidence + reason + stale flag), embed status, and enrichment_state. REUSE: both surfaces consume ONE shared read seam — a view-model (lode-ay5.1) built on lode.display (display_annotations/display_edges, the shared stale-display seam lode-npx.4) — so they cannot drift; no re-deriving the display policy. PARITY (decision 2026-07-08): CONTENT parity, FORMAT differs — the view-model carries every field (incl. edge reason+confidence and enrichment_state); the modal renders expanded (e.g. a confidence bar), 'lode show' renders compact; the guard checks the same FIELDS are surfaced on both, NOT byte-identical output. CLI (decision 2026-07-08): no new command, but 'lode show' GROWS to the view-model's field set — it gains edge reason+confidence (compact) and the enrichment_state line, neither of which it prints today. STATE (decision 2026-07-08): enrichment_state is three-valued {pending, ready, failed} keyed on the HEAD version, so a not-yet-enriched note reads 'pending', a dead-lettered enrich job reads 'failed' (not a misleading empty), and stale-flagged content is always shown alongside (pending + stale coexist).
acceptance_criteria: From Browse (F3), 'i' on a highlighted note opens a modal showing that note's summary/tags/entities/inferred-edges(confidence+reason+stale)/embed-status/enrichment_state, dismissable with Esc, scrolling when content exceeds the viewport; the capture screen is unchanged; the modal renders via the shared view-model (lode-ay5.1, built on lode.display — no second copy of the stale-display policy); 'lode show' is at CONTENT parity with the modal — same field set (incl. edge reason+confidence, which it must GAIN, and a three-valued enrichment_state distinguishing pending / failed / enriched-empty), formatted for the CLI rather than byte-identical; a parity check asserts both surfaces expose the same view-model fields. All children closed.
notes:
CRITICISM (debate 2026-07-08):
1. DESCRIPTION premise is FALSE: 'lode show' does NOT surface edges 'with reason+confidence'. cli.show_ prints only '-> {to_id}[stale]' (no reason, no confidence), though both columns exist in the edges table. Fix the DESCRIPTION.
2. Parity contradiction (CRUX): the modal acceptance shows edges(confidence+reason+stale); the CLI shows neither today. 'Parity' is underspecified — either the CLI grows to print reason+confidence (a net-new user-visible CLI change that contradicts ay5.3's 'thin refactor'/'that's all on that side'), or the modal drops them. DECISION NEEDED before ay5.1's EnrichmentView shape is frozen.
3. 'Parity guard' is aspirational: ay5.2 and ay5.3 each test their own surface against the view-model, but nothing diffs the two surfaces against each other. The edge gap in (1) would pass both suites while the surfaces visibly diverge. Make the guard concrete: a shared render helper both call, OR a test enumerating view-model fields that asserts each appears on both surfaces.
DECISION (2026-07-08, note 2 resolved): 'Content parity, format differs.' EnrichmentView CARRIES reason+confidence; each surface renders as fits its medium (modal expanded w/ confidence bar+reason; CLI compact e.g. '-> to_id (reason, 0.82)'). The parity guard checks SAME FIELDS surfaced, not byte-identical output (resolves note 3 toward a field-coverage test, not a shared render helper). ay5.3 still gains edge reason+confidence (compact) — not a pure thin refactor.

title: Define the land-escalated resolution transition in /land
description:
Define the RESOLUTION TRANSITION for a `land-escalated` branch in `/land`. This is the
one genuine upstream gap the `/debate` pass surfaced.

## The gap
`/land` sets the `land-escalated` label and KEEPS the branch "until the human resolves
it" (land/SKILL.md "Escalate" section). But NO skill defines HOW a human resolves it —
there is no transition that REMOVES `land-escalated`. Contrast: `human`-labeled decision
tickets self-clear via `bd human respond` / `bd human dismiss`. `land-escalated` has no
such exit, so `bd list --label land-escalated` grows MONOTONICALLY. The forthcoming
`/sweep` surfacer will show a queue that never drains (it won't re-notify resolved
items, but the list accumulates zombies).

## What "done" looks like
A documented, mechanical resolution path (in land/SKILL.md, and mirrored into
docs/agents-workflow.md) for each way a `land-escalated` can end, e.g.:
- Human decides the branch SHOULD land as-is → swap `land-escalated` back to
  `ready-for-land` (re-enters the lander), OR
- Human decides it must be rebuilt → `bd supersede` into a fresh rebuild ticket (drop
  the branch), OR
- Human decides to drop it → close with reason (GC the branch).

Pick the minimal, consistent set. The key invariant: after a human acts, the ticket
NO LONGER carries `land-escalated`, so the surfacer's queue drains.

## Notes
- This is independent of `/sweep` (real hole today), but `/sweep`'s usefulness depends
  on it — surface a queue that can actually empty.
- Keep it consistent with the existing bounce/needs-rebase transitions in land/SKILL.md.
- Decision belongs in docs/ (agents-workflow.md / decisions.md), not just the ticket.
acceptance_criteria: land/SKILL.md (and docs/agents-workflow.md) document a mechanical path for every way a land-escalated resolves, each ending with the land-escalated label REMOVED so bd list --label land-escalated can reach empty. Consistent with existing bounce/needs-rebase transitions. Decision recorded in docs/.
notes:
CRITICISM (/debate 2026-07-08):
1. 'LAND AS-IS' EXIT RE-ESCALATES IN A LOOP (correctness gap). One proposed exit is 'human decides it should land as-is -> swap land-escalated back to ready-for-land'. But a branch reaches land-escalated precisely because land-review found a genuine decision only a human can make (ticket ambiguous about 'done', etc.). If the human just swaps the label back with nothing else changed, /land's first task re-runs land-review, hits the SAME ambiguity, and escalates AGAIN — an infinite escalate<->ready loop. The transition is only correct if the human's decision is MATERIALIZED so land-review won't re-trip: either (a) human edits the ticket to remove the ambiguity, or (b) an explicit 'human-blessed, skip semantic re-review and land' fast-path that /land honors. The naive label-swap is NOT a complete transition. RESOLVE: .2 must specify which. [DECISION PENDING - surfaced to human]
DECISION (human, 2026-07-08) — Finding #1 RESOLVED: the 'land as-is' exit requires the human to MATERIALIZE the resolution in the ticket (edit the acceptance/'done' criteria to remove the ambiguity land-review flagged) BEFORE swapping land-escalated -> ready-for-land, so re-review passes cleanly. land-review stays authoritative — NO 'human-blessed' bypass label. Rationale (human): 'make this difficult; if I can't convince the AI to proceed, a JFDI should be a manual override' — i.e. forcing a land past land-review is an out-of-band manual act, not a designed fast-path. So the documented resolution set is: (a) materialize-fix -> ready-for-land, (b) supersede -> rebuild (drop branch), (c) close -> drop (GC branch); each ends with land-escalated REMOVED. DOC IMPACT: add the land-escalated resolution transitions to the label/state diagram + text in land/SKILL.md and docs/agents-workflow.md (record in .4).

title: Build /sweep — human-decision surfacer (surface-only)
description:
Build `/sweep` — the third `/loop` leg, a SURFACE-ONLY human-decision surfacer. It
scans `bd` for work that has stopped waiting on a human and nothing else consumes,
dedups it, and actively surfaces it (PushNotification + a running digest issue). It
writes no `trunk`, makes no decisions, dispatches no builders. It is the observability
layer that makes running `/code` + `/land` + `/epic-audit` unattended safe.

## Why (verified gap)
`/code` sweeps `needs-rebase`; `/land` bounces re-enter `bd ready`; `/epic-audit` runs
itself as `/loop /epic-audit`. The only pipeline outputs with NO downstream consumer
are the ones parked for a human:
- `land-escalated` label (set by `/land` escalate, incl. rebase-conflict) — queryable
  via `bd list --label land-escalated` — consumed by NOTHING.
- `human`-labeled `decision` ticket (set by `/epic-audit` escalate) — `bd human list`
  — only a human, manually.
- epic `epic-audited` + open + all children closed (`/epic-audit` never closes epics)
  — derived query — surfaced by NOTHING.

## Scope (in)
1. Surface the human-decision queue: `bd list --label land-escalated` ∪ `bd human list`.
   Notify on NEW items only; keep ONE running digest issue of the full current queue.
2. Surface epics ready for a human close-decision: type=epic ∧ status=open ∧
   labels ⊇ {epic-audited} ∧ every parent-child child closed.

## Non-goals (invariants — hold the line)
- Never writes `trunk` (that is `/land` alone).
- Never builds/lands/audits — not `/code`, `/land`, `/epic-audit`. NO audit dispatch
  (already `/loop /epic-audit`).
- Never makes/auto-defaults the human's decision — surface only (escalation-autonomy /
  wait-when-away norms).
- Does not own the livelock caps (deferred; see epic Design).
- Does not touch `.beads/issues.jsonl` (import.auto:false invariant, lode-6ra).

## Per-pass algorithm
```
1. bd dolt pull
2. queue = bd list --label land-escalated  ∪  bd human list
3. closable = epics(type=epic ∧ open ∧ labels⊇{epic-audited} ∧ all children closed)
4. current = queue ∪ closable
   last = read prior "human-decision digest" issue body   # DEDUP STORE = the digest issue itself
   new  = current − last
   if new ≠ ∅:
     upsert the digest issue with `current`               # Dolt-durable, cross-machine
     PushNotification summarizing `new`
     bd dolt push
5. report one line: queue depth, N new, M closable
```

## DECIDED (from debate)
- Dedup state lives IN the digest issue (Dolt-durable, travels cross-machine). A
  scratchpad state file re-notifies the whole queue from a second machine — REJECTED.
- This collapses "is it even a skill?" — the digest upsert + derived close-ready query
  justify a small skill; the state has a home (the issue), not a scratchpad file.

## Cadence
`/loop 30m /sweep` — escalations are exceptions, epics complete rarely; slow tick is fine.

## Dependency note (soft, not a hard blocker)
Without child #2 (`land-escalated` resolution transition) the surfaced queue never
DRAINS — `/sweep` still works (surfaces + dedups) but shows a growing list. Build order
preference: #2 before or with this, but this does not hard-block on it.
acceptance_criteria: Empty queue + no closable epics => clean no-op (no write, no notify). A new land-escalated/human item notifies exactly once; same queue next pass notifies nothing; resolved item drops out. A close-ready epic (epic-audited+open+all children closed) surfaced exactly once. Dedup survives across machines (state in the digest issue). Never writes trunk, dispatches no builder/lander/auditor, never touches .beads/issues.jsonl. A failing sub-step reports and the loop survives.
notes:
EMBEDDED DRAFT SPEC (verbatim, source of record — replaces scratchpad/sweep-spec.md):

# `/sweep` — human-decision surfacer (SPEC, pre-debate, v2)

**Status:** proposal, not built. Written to be stress-tested by `/debate`.
**v2 change:** verified against `.claude/skills/land/SKILL.md` and
`.claude/skills/epic-audit/SKILL.md`. The audit-dispatch leg is **dropped**
(already covered by `/loop /epic-audit`); escalation markers confirmed to exist;
scope narrowed to a near-read-only surfacer.

## One-liner

The third `/loop` leg. It scans `bd` for work that has **stopped waiting on a
human** and nothing else consumes — land/audit escalations, and epics ready for
a human close-decision — dedups them, and **actively surfaces** them
(PushNotification + a running digest). It writes no `trunk`, makes no decisions,
and dispatches no builders. It is the observability layer that makes running
`/code` + `/land` + `/epic-audit` unattended safe.

## Why it exists (verified gap)

`/code` sweeps `needs-rebase`; `/land` bounces re-enter `bd ready`; `/epic-audit`
runs itself as `/loop /epic-audit`. The only pipeline outputs with **no
downstream consumer** are the ones parked for a human:

| Human-parked signal | Set by | Queryable via | Consumed today |
|---|---|---|---|
| `land-escalated` label | `/land` escalate (incl. rebase-conflict) | `bd list --label land-escalated` | **nothing** ✗ |
| `human`-labeled `decision` ticket | `/epic-audit` escalate | `bd human list` | only a human manually ✗ |
| epic `epic-audited` + open + all children closed | `/epic-audit` (never closes epics) | derived query | **nothing** ✗ |

All three sit silent until a human happens to look. `/sweep` turns them into an
active ping.

## What changed after reading the skills (do NOT re-litigate in debate)

- **Audit dispatch dropped.** Bare `/epic-audit` is already a sweep (prefers
  `epic-ready-to-audit`, no-ops when none). Use `/loop 30m /epic-audit`; `/sweep`
  does not audit.
- **Audit regeneration loop does not exist.** `epic-audited` is terminal and
  excluded from both `/epic-audit`'s filter and `/land`'s re-flag guard. Auditing
  is once-per-epic. No cap needed.
- **Escalation markers confirmed present** — `land-escalated` and the `human`
  label. Leg B has real inputs; the earlier "no queryable marker" blocker is void.

## Responsibilities (in scope)

1. **Surface the human-decision queue.** Collect `bd list --label land-escalated`
   + `bd human list`. Notify on **new** items only; keep a single running digest
   of the full current queue.
2. **Surface epics ready for a human close-decision.** Epics that are
   `epic-audited`, still `open`, with every `parent-child` child closed —
   `/epic-audit` leaves these for the human and nothing else flags them.

## Non-goals (invariants — hold the line in debate)

- **Never writes `trunk`** (that is `/land` alone).
- **Never builds, lands, or audits** — not `/code`, `/land`, or `/epic-audit`.
- **Never makes or auto-defaults the human's decision** — surface only. Honors
  the escalation-autonomy / wait-when-away norms.
- **Does not own the livelock caps.** The bounce-lineage cap belongs in `/land`,
  the rebase-attempt cap in `/code`. `/sweep` only makes their escalations visible.
- **Does not touch `.beads/issues.jsonl`** (no add/commit/import — `import.auto:
  false` invariant, lode-6ra).

## Per-pass algorithm

```
1. bd dolt pull                              # fresh state (Dolt authoritative)
2. queue = bd list --label land-escalated  ∪  bd human list
3. closable_epics = epics where type=epic ∧ status=open
                    ∧ labels ⊇ {epic-audited}
                    ∧ all parent-child children closed
4. current = queue ∪ closable_epics
   new = current − last_surfaced          # dedup on stable IDs
   if new ≠ ∅:
     upsert ONE "human-decision digest" issue with `current` (full queue)
     PushNotification summarizing `new`
     persist last_surfaced := current      # durable store (see open Q)
5. report one line: queue depth, N new surfaced, M epics closable
```

No `bd dolt push` is required if `/sweep` writes no bd state (see dedup-store
question). If it upserts a digest issue, push after.

## Outputs / side effects

- **Near read-only.** Optional single digest issue (upserted in place) + a
  PushNotification on the delta. No trunk write, no merge, no GC, no builder
  dispatch. This is deliberately the lowest-privilege leg of the three.

## Termination & convergence (the reason `/sweep` earns its place)

Verified state of the 3-loop system:

- **Provably convergent:** the land/close path (monotone `bd close`) and the
  audit leg (`epic-audited` terminal, excluded from re-flag + sweep). No revert
  flip-flop exists — the one true revert hazard (jsonl auto-import reverting a
  close) is mutexed off in `/land` (`import.auto:false`, `restore
  --staged --worktree`, push-then-close-then-dolt-push ordering).
- **Residual non-terminating edges** (both route to a human-escape valve, both
  currently silent — which is `/sweep`'s justification):
  1. **Bounce rebuild chain** — `/land` bounce → supersede + rebuild ticket →
     `/code` rebuild → bounce again for the same reason → unbounded supersede
     chain. No lineage cap today. *Fix lives in `/land`* (cap lineage depth →
     escalate `land-escalated`); `/sweep` surfaces the escalation.
  2. **needs-rebase starvation** — only under *perpetual* trunk churn; a finite
     backlog quiesces, and a real rebase conflict escapes to `land-escalated`.
     Low priority; optional attempt-cap in `/code`.

So `/sweep` does not make the system converge — the caps do — but it makes the
non-convergent cases **visible** the moment they escalate, which is what lets you
run all three loops unattended.

## Cadence

`/loop 30m /sweep`. Escalations are exceptions and epics complete rarely; a slow
tick is fine and keeps cache-warmth irrelevant.

## Open design questions (FOR DEBATE)

1. **Surface channel.** PushNotification + digest issue vs. transcript-only vs.
   `bd`-native report. Which actually reaches a non-watching human, and is a
   digest *issue* worth the one bd write (and the `bd dolt push` it forces)?
2. **Dedup store.** Scratchpad state file (ephemeral, per-machine) vs. a durable
   `bd` marker. If `/sweep` may run on a different machine than last time, the
   `last_surfaced` set must be durable, else it re-notifies the whole queue.
3. **Should `/sweep` exist as its own skill at all,** or is it thin enough to be
   a `/loop`-able one-liner query + notify? Counter-argument for a skill: the
   dedup state and the digest-issue upsert want a stable home.
4. **Do the livelock caps get built alongside `/sweep`** (in `/land` and
   `/code`), or is surfacing-only acceptable for v1 on the bet that bounce-chains
   are rare? `/sweep` makes them survivable-but-visible; the caps make them
   impossible. Sequencing call.

## Acceptance criteria

- `/sweep` with an empty human-decision queue and no closable epics is a clean
  no-op — no write, no notification.
- A new `land-escalated` / `human` item triggers exactly one notification; a
  subsequent pass with the same queue notifies nothing; a resolved item drops out.
- An `epic-audited` + open + all-children-closed epic is surfaced as
  "ready to close" exactly once.
- `/sweep` never writes `trunk`, never dispatches a builder/lander/auditor, and
  never touches `.beads/issues.jsonl`.
- A failing sub-step reports and the `/loop` survives to the next tick.
CRITICISM (/debate 2026-07-08):
1. DIGEST-ISSUE IDENTITY UNDEFINED (blocker). The dedup design rests on upsert 'THE' digest issue + read 'the prior' digest body, but nothing specifies how /sweep FINDS that same issue next pass, esp. cross-machine. bd create mints a random ID; remembering it in scratchpad is the per-machine state the debate REJECTED. So it must be found by a durable query (reserved label e.g. sweep-digest, or title match) — unspecified in spec + acceptance. First-run bootstrap (no digest -> create) vs steady-state (find -> update) also unspecified. Two builders will guess differently. RESOLVE: name a reserved locator label + specify find-or-create bootstrap in acceptance. [DECISION PENDING - surfaced to human]
2. 'if new != empty' GUARD LEAVES RESOLVED ITEMS STALE (contradicts acceptance). Algorithm only upserts digest when new != empty. A pass whose ONLY change is a removal (item resolved, nothing added) has new = empty, so digest is NOT rewritten and shows the zombie until the next ADD triggers a rewrite. But acceptance says 'a resolved item drops out' — it doesn't, promptly. FIX: rewrite digest whenever current != last (add OR remove); only NOTIFY when new != empty. Separate the two triggers.
3. SOFT-DEP NOTE CONTRADICTS HARD DEP EDGE. Description calls the dep on .2 'soft, not a hard blocker', but the bd graph has .2 BLOCKING .1 (hard) — /code won't schedule .1 until .2 closes. Text and graph disagree; graph wins at dispatch. RESOLVE: drop the hard dep (keep as preferred-order note) OR delete the 'soft' language. [DECISION PENDING - surfaced to human]
4. SURFACE-CHANNEL DELIVERY UNVERIFIED (see also .4). Spec open Q#1 (which channel reaches a NON-WATCHING human) was listed FOR DEBATE but only the dedup-store half got resolved. Whether PushNotification from an unattended /loop /sweep actually reaches an away human is never confirmed, yet scope+acceptance hardcode it. If it only renders in an unwatched transcript, /sweep degrades to 'writes a bd issue nobody sees'. RESOLVE: verify PushNotification delivery semantics BEFORE build; make acceptance assert delivery-to-away-human, not just 'a notification was emitted.'
DECISION (human, 2026-07-08) — Finding #1 RESOLVED: digest locator = a RESERVED LABEL (e.g. sweep-digest). /sweep queries bd list --label sweep-digest; 0 rows -> create + add-label (bootstrap); 1 row -> update; >1 -> surface duplicate + stop. Rationale: it is another label but its purpose is clear w.r.t. the label/state diagram. DOC IMPACT: the new sweep-digest label must be added to the label/state diagram + label glossary in docs/agents-workflow.md (record in .4).
DECISION (human, 2026-07-08) — Finding #3 RESOLVED: the dep on .2 is HARD (keep the graph edge; .2 blocks .1). /sweep ships only once the queue can drain. The 'Dependency note (soft, not a hard blocker)' paragraph in this ticket's DESCRIPTION is VOID/superseded — treat .2 as a hard blocker. (Kept as a superseding note rather than rewriting the long embedded description; builder should honor this note over the description prose.)

title: Stop mirroring httpx 200-OK lines to the console (work/ask); errors only
description: specs/03-tui-features.md item 4. The anthropic SDK's httpx transport logs 'HTTP Request: POST ... 200 OK' at INFO on the 'httpx' logger, which the root console handler mirrors to stderr during 'work'/'ask'. The end user doesn't need to see 200s. In src/lode/logconfig.configure_logging, raise the 'httpx' logger to WARNING for console output (keep lode's own INFO), so successful requests are silent and only httpx WARNING+/errors surface. Apply globally (every command benefits), not just work/ask. Confirm the file handler still records what's useful for debugging.
acceptance_criteria: 'lode ask'/'lode work' no longer print httpx 2xx lines to stderr; the file handler (lode.log) STILL records httpx 200 lines; an httpx WARNING+/error still surfaces on the console; lode's own INFO console lines are unaffected.
notes: MECHANISM (decided 2026-07-06): do NOT bump the 'httpx' logger level — that would strip 200s from the file handler too. Instead attach a logging.Filter to the CONSOLE/stream handler only that drops httpx INFO records (name.startswith('httpx') and levelno < WARNING), leaving the file handler (tagged _lode_file in logconfig) untouched so lode.log keeps the 200s for debugging. In logconfig.configure_logging: the stream handler is the one basicConfig installs on root; add the filter there (and note the TUI's console=False path removes stream handlers entirely, so the filter is a console-only concern). httpx WARNING+/errors still reach the console.

metadata.land_summary: Console-only logging.Filter drops httpx sub-WARNING records (200-OK lines) from the stream handler; file handler (lode.log) untouched, lode's own INFO and httpx WARNING+/errors still surface.

title: work: --wait option that blocks until submitted jobs are processed (bounded)
description: specs/03-tui-features.md item 3. Add a 'lode work --wait' (a.k.a. --until-done) option that polls — reconcile + drain + batch-collect — until no pending/running jobs remain, so the user doesn't have to re-run 'work' to see async (Batches API) enrich jobs land. Bound it with a timeout ('up to some reasonable time') so it can't hang forever on a stuck batch; on timeout, exit non-zero with a clear message naming the still-in-flight jobs. Reuse the existing --loop/--interval machinery and WorkerLock in cli.work; the difference from --loop is the exit-when-drained condition + timeout. Default timeout should be configurable via Settings (docs/configuration.md) with a sensible default.
acceptance_criteria: 'lode work --wait' returns only once the queue is fully drained (incl. batch enrich results collected) or the timeout fires; on timeout it exits non-zero and names the outstanding jobs; without --wait behaviour is unchanged (one-shot).
notes: DESIGN DECISION (async latency, 2026-07-06): --wait is bounded and MAY legitimately time out on slow enrich batches (Batches API can take minutes-to-hours) — this is accepted, not a bug. On timeout with jobs in-flight, exit non-zero and NAME the outstanding jobs (as specified). Document in help text / docs that --wait suits embed-heavy or small-batch cases, and that large async enrich loads may need a re-run. Do NOT switch enrich to the synchronous _enrich_handler fallback under --wait. ---- TERMINATION INVARIANT (verified against worker.py): batch-submitted enrich jobs stay status='running' with batch_handle set and are EXCLUDED from _reclaim_stale_running; they only flip running->done when a later drain's _batch_collect_enrich pre-step polls the ended batch. So the 'no pending/running jobs remain' condition is correct ONLY because _batch_collect_enrich (top of every drain) eventually completes them. Do NOT dead-letter or reclaim in-flight batch jobs in the wait loop.

metadata.land_summary: Add 'lode work --wait' (--until-done): polls reconcile+drain until the queue drains or Settings.work_wait_timeout_s (default 1800s) elapses, then exits non-zero naming outstanding jobs; rejects --wait+--loop; adds work_wait_timeout_s knob (config.py + docs/configuration.md).

title: CLI: 'lode show <id>' — per-note detail incl. derived enrichment
description: specs/03-tui-features.md item 2 (chosen surface: on-demand introspection). Add 'lode show <id>' printing a note's head body plus its derived enrichment: summary, tags, entities, inferred edges (annotations table kind in summary/tag/entity where source='ai' status='fresh' source_version=head; edges table from_id=note_id source='ai'), and embed/index status (passages present?). Accepts the same unambiguous-prefix id resolution as purge (see the purge-prefix ticket — share the resolver). Read-only; Typer/echo style consistent with status/jobs/egress.
acceptance_criteria: 'lode show <id-or-prefix>' prints the note body + its tags/entities/summary/edges + whether it is embedded; an un-enriched note shows empty/absent enrichment gracefully; unknown/ambiguous id errors like purge.
notes: Reuse Repository.resolve_note_prefix from lode-1gr.3 (live-notes-only candidate set, exit-1 on unknown/ambiguous) — do not re-implement id resolution here. 'lode show' is read-only. SHORT-ID: use the shared 8-char note-id abbreviation (see lode-1gr.2) for any abbreviated refs; version-id digests use cli._short (12).

metadata.land_summary: Add 'lode show <id-or-prefix>': read-only per-note detail printing head body + derived enrichment (summary/tags/entities/edges via the shared lode.display stale-flag policy) + embed status; shares purge's resolve_note_prefix (unknown/ambiguous errors identically); un-enriched notes show '(none)' sections. Prints full ids (no abbreviation), consistent with 'lode notes'.

title: work: print a per-job outcome summary of what enrichment/embedding produced
description: specs/03-tui-features.md item 2 (chosen surface: in-flow work summary). Today 'lode work' only prints 'drained N job(s)' — the user can't tell what enrichment did. Have work report, per processed job, what happened: e.g. 'enriched <short-id>: 4 tags, 2 entities, 3 edges, summary set' and 'embedded <short-id>: 3 passages'. enrich_version already logs these counts (src/lode/enrich.py: 'enrich_version: version=.. tags=.. entities=.. edges=.. summary=..'); the async/batch path lands via lode.worker.drain + collect_enrich_batch. Surface the counts through the drain return path to cli.work's echo rather than relying on log lines. Coordinate with the httpx-quiet ticket so this stays readable.
acceptance_criteria: A drain pass that COLLECTS a completed enrich batch prints a human-readable per-note line (tags/entities/edges/summary); a drain pass that runs embed jobs prints a per-note passage-count line; a no-op drain still prints the existing 'drained 0 job(s)'. Note: a one-shot 'work' immediately after capture only submits the enrich batch, so the enrich line appears on a subsequent pass (or under 'work --wait', lode-1gr.6).
notes: SEAM CORRECTION (verified against worker.py): enrichment is async-batch. drain() returns int (main claim-run loop only) and its docstring notes batch pre-step activity is NOT in the return count. So there are TWO channels, not one 'drain return path': (a) EMBED counts land synchronously via run_one in the main loop; (b) ENRICH counts land on a LATER drain via the _batch_collect_enrich pre-step (batch results). The function is _batch_collect_enrich (private), NOT 'collect_enrich_batch'. Emit the enrich summary from the collect pass, not the submit pass. Depends on lode-1gr.6 (--wait) because that is what makes enrich outcomes observable within one command; a bare one-shot work only SUBMITS the batch and prints 'drained 0 job(s)'.

metadata.land_summary: lode work now prints a per-job outcome line (embedded <id>: N passages; enriched <id>: T tags, E entities, G edges, summary set/empty) ahead of 'drained N job(s)', via an additive opt-in outcomes sink threaded through run_one/drain/_batch_collect_enrich/collect_enrich_batch + shared enrich.format_enrich_outcome; drain()'s int return preserved.

title: purge: accept an unambiguous note-id prefix, not just the full 36-char id
description: specs/03-tui-features.md item 1 (ergonomics). With Browse/notes showing short ids, requiring the full UUID for 'lode purge' is hostile. Let 'lode purge <prefix>' resolve an unambiguous note_id prefix to the full id before delegating to Repository.purge (src/lode/cli.py purge + src/lode/repository.py). A prefix matching zero notes -> clear 'no such note' error (exit 1, as today); a prefix matching >1 note -> 'ambiguous' error listing the candidates (exit 1); exactly one match -> purge it. Full ids must still work unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: 'lode purge <unique-prefix>' purges the right note; ambiguous prefix errors and lists candidates without deleting; unknown prefix errors; full-id purge behaviour is unchanged.
notes: SCOPE (decided 2026-07-06): add a REUSABLE, unit-tested resolver in repository.py — e.g. Repository.resolve_note_prefix(prefix) -> full note_id — do NOT inline it in cli.purge. lode-1gr.5 ('lode show') shares this exact resolver (it depends on this ticket). CANDIDATE SET = LIVE notes only (same v.op != 'delete' filter list_notes/Browse use): a prefix resolves only what the user can see via 'lode notes'/Browse; a tombstoned note is NOT reachable by prefix. A FULL 36-char id must still purge regardless of state (unchanged from today). Zero live matches -> 'no such note' (exit 1); >1 -> 'ambiguous', list candidates (exit 1); exactly one -> purge.

metadata.land_summary: purge (and future 'lode show') accept an unambiguous live-note-id prefix via reusable Repository.resolve_note_prefix + AmbiguousNoteIdError; full-id bypass preserved; empty/zero/ambiguous prefixes error clearly (exit 1)

title: CLI: 'lode notes' — list live notes with id, date, summary

Add a 'lode notes' command that lists every live note with its full note_id, a short human-readable date, and its summary (head kind='summary' annotation, falling back to the note's first line — same rule as lode.tui.browse._head_summary).
